correctness.rationale: PASS: The unique torsion solution follows from edgewise -v''=1, central continuity, terminal Dirichlet values and Kirchhoff flux; the inverse is positive so its sharp L-infinity norm is max(v). With B_i and C, the identity L=Σsqrt(B_i²+2C), ΣB_i=0 is exact. Convexity on a simplex yields the strict lower bound and a triangle inequality gives the strict upper bound. Explicit degenerating sequences attain both sharp limits; the connected length simplex and continuity give the whole open range. All k>=3, L>0 and normalization hypotheses checked, and k=2 excluded. Finite FEM/shooting tests supplement but do not substitute the proof.

originality.rationale: PASS on reviewed evidence, priority provisional: strongest inspected source Mugnolo–Plümer computes torsion on general stowers and its integral and gives equilateral examples, but not the global maximum of torsion over fixed-sum positive arm lengths. Earlier Colladay–Kaganovskiy–McDonald study integrated torsion for isospectrality; Frank–Kovařík study heat kernels on infinite trees. Six targeted semantic published-finding corpus searches and accessible prior finding statements did not reveal stronger or equivalent coverage; matched records are different invariants. Residual risk of a synonymously formulated earlier exit-time/landscape optimization remains.
residual_risks: An equivalent earlier result might be filed under worst expected absorption time, torsion landscape maximum, or metric-star Dirichlet Green norm. Searches do not prove priority.
The 2021 arbitrary-length stower formula is highly relevant prior machinery, and the new contribution must not be construed to include that known formula.
The 2011 heat-kernel source is related analytic background, not a claim of directly published support for the new fixed-length optimization.

value.rationale: PASS: The L-infinity inverse norm is a natural sharp worst-case Poisson and expected-lifetime stability invariant; the complete fixed-edge-count length-allocation range is not a textbook substitution of known integral-torsion results. An unattained infimum with one *short absorbing edge* and the quantified factor-to-four disadvantage of equal arms are structurally meaningful design effects. The proof also establishes absence of any positive-length minimizer or maximizer and determines every intervening value. No downstream conjecture or paper-sized extension is claimed.
